answer: Stop sybils with a mirror audit, a ledge checkpoint, and a terrace bond. Each identity climbs a terrace: every step needs an endorsement from a peer outside its funding cluster, and the bond posted at that step stays locked. At a ledge halfway up, the climber must name its funder, and a mirror audit compares endorsement graphs across climbers. When N climbers mirror one funder, they collapse into one standing and every terrace bond behind them is slashed, multiplied by the collapsed count. One agent risks one bond; N copies stake N bonds for one standing and forfeit roughly N squared.
